0,3,1: Week 1 - LP targeting and Fund III positioning
0,4,1:
Luke Badiali (BeDeveloped)
Richard Hale (Senior Partner)
Natalie Grieve (Investor Relations Director)
1,0,1: First session with Richard and Natalie on who Fund III should be raised from and how Westbourne is positioned. We agreed a target LP profile, three LP segments with re-ups carrying most of the raise, and a specialist rather than generalist position. Fund size is still with the partners and a first-close fee discount was rejected.
5,1,1: Write the Fund III narrative for LPs around the specialist positioning.
5,2,1: Bring the current Fund III draft deck and the Fund II track record summary.
2,1,1: Natalie said Fund II closed at £320m from 22 LPs. Most have said informally they will look at Fund III but none has committed.
2,2,1: Richard said LPs keep asking whether Westbourne is a healthcare fund, an education fund or a generalist. The current deck tries to be all three.
2,3,1: Richard wants to go to market at £450m. Natalie is concerned that is a big step up from Fund II with a thin new LP list.
3,1,1: Target UK and European pension funds and fund-of-funds with over £2bn AUM and an existing mid-market buy-out allocation, at tickets of £15m to £40m.
3,2,1: Work three LP segments: Fund II re-ups (aiming for 60% of the raise), new institutional LPs and single family offices.
3,3,1: Position Westbourne as a specialist healthcare services and education buy-out manager, not a generalist mid-market fund.
3,6,1: Set the Fund III target at £450m with a hard cap of £550m.
3,7,1: Offer a 25bps management fee discount to LPs committing at first close.
4,1,0: Take the £450m target and £550m hard cap to the partners meeting
4,2,0: Rank Fund II LPs by likelihood to re-up
